title: Traffic Tilt Balance Canvas and Preflight Checklists — Aug 2027 (draft)
body:
Context:
This doc is a lightweight operator-facing canvas and checklist for performing a traffic-tilt style rollout across model variants / regions / capacity tiers. It focuses on small incremental changes (tilts) rather than single-step cutovers. Use this when we need deterministic latency/cost/eval control and want quick rollback windows.

Audience:
- Release engineers running the shift
- SREs monitoring latency/availability
- Product owners watching quality regressions
- Solutions engineers validating client-facing behavior

Goals (what success looks like):
- No customer-visible errors during tilt steps (error rate < 0.05%)
- Latency P95 stays within SLO band for 95% of tilt steps
- Quality regression score (prompt set diffs) below configured threshold
- Rollback path validated and rehearsed within 15 minutes

High-level tilt plan (example):
- Start: Baseline traffic on model-v2 (stable) at 100%
- Step 1 (T+0): 5% -> model-v3-canary (region us-west-2) for 30m
- Step 2 (T+30m): 10% -> model-v3-canary (total 15%) for 30m
- Step 3 (T+60m): 25% -> model-v3-canary for 45m (observe burst metrics)
- Step 4 (T+105m): 50% -> model-v3-canary for 1h (longer soak)
- Step 5 (T+~3h): 100% -> model-v3-std (promote and drain canary nodes)

Notes: timings are flexible. Use the tilt controller to schedule and auto-pause on gate triggers.

Preflight checklist (operator quick-run):
- [ ] Confirm release window and pager rotation (list on the calendar)
- [ ] Notify customer-success of potential rate/latency blips (channel: #cs-ops)
- [ ] Validate infra capacity: node pool autoscaler active and headroom >= 30%
- [ ] Validate K8s node taints/affinities for canary group: labels present
- [ ] Confirm canary model image/checksum matches release branch PR#678
- [ ] Run canary dry-run against synthetic traffic (local harness): pass smoke tests
- [ ] Confirm telemetry is flowing: traces, request logs, kv cache hit metrics
- [ ] Confirm alert thresholds for tilt gates are set in PagerDuty (latency/err/budget)

Tilt-step operator play (for each percentage step):
1) Kick tilt via controller with note on channel (#releases). Include timestamp and ticket id.
2) Start stopwatch and mark expected observation window.
3) Run quick smoke: 10 synthetic prompts across 3 sequences (short/med/long).
4) Observe metrics for the window (see observability checklist below).
5) If all gates green -> proceed to next step. If any gate trips -> escalate and perform rollback.

Observability checklist (during each step):
- Error rate (500/502/timeout) -> absolute and delta from baseline
- Token-level cost delta (to track unexpected quantization or throughput regressions)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by region and model variant
- Throughput (requests/s) and queue lengths on serving runtime
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix-hit distribution
- Model tail losses (per-client topk regressions) captured by eval hooks
- Feature flags / routing policy audits (ensure correct route used)

Gate thresholds (suggested):
- Error rate increase > 0.03% absolute or > 300% relative -> PAUSE
- Latency p95 increase > 150ms absolute or +30% relative -> PAUSE
- Token-cost increase > 15% -> PAUSE and investigate
- Quality regression (eval harness) delta > 0.05 -> PAUSE and triage

Rollback decision tree (fast):
- If any PAUSE condition met in first 2 steps: immediate rollback to last known good (usually 0% for canary) and notify #releases and PD
- If PAUSE at later step (>25%): roll back to previous healthy step percentage (e.g., 25% -> 10%) and open incident runbook
- If repeated instability after rollback: full abort and attach logs/trace ids to JIRA-RELEASE-8901

Post-tilt stabilization (after 100%):
- Leave telemetry sampling high for 2 hours
- Run the full eval suite on live traffic captures (sample 0.1%)
- Kick off cost reconciliation job for the day to compare expected unit economics
- Update rollout notes and mark release as GA in console when green

Release notes draft (to include in public changelog and internal digest):
- Short blurb: "model-v3: Improved context-aware summarization and latency improvements under typical web workloads. Rolled out via staged traffic-tilt across regions — canary started 2027-08-10."
- Known limitations: "Batching behavior for sequences >2k tokens may show higher p99; ongoing tuning scheduled. Some customers on dedicated pools may need quantization profile flip; see support KB."
- Impact: "Most users should see equal or better latency and quality; contact support with 'release: model-v3' in subject if you see regressions."

Operator notes & shorthand (notes to self):
- Keep tilt steps small if traffic is bursty (use 2.5% steps overnight)
- Watch for region-local cache warming causing temporary latency dips -> ignore if bounded <5m
- If kv-cache hit ratio drops suddenly, suspect stale prefix cache on serving nodes after deploy
- Have a pre-authz rollback script ready: scripts/tilt-rollback.sh --fast (PR referenced above)

Calendar / shift template (example for a 6-hour window):
- T-60m: Preflight and dry-run (owner: Priya)
- T-30m: Pager rotate + announce (owner: Ethan)
- T-0: Step 1 (5%) start (owner: Liam)
- T+30m: Step 2 (10%) (owner: Liam)
- T+60m: Step 3 (25%) (owner: Ethan)
- T+105m: Step 4 (50%) (owner: Priya)
- T+165m: Step 5 (100%) (owner: Priya)
- T+195m: Stabilize & eval run (owner: María)

Quick command cheatsheet:
- Tilt controller: tiltctl shift --to model-v3-canary --pct 5 --note "tilt step 5%"
- Rollback: tiltctl rollback --to-percentage 0 --fast --reason "err-rate"
- Smoke harness: tests/smoke/tilt-smoke.sh --region us-west-2 --iterations 10
- Telemetry pin: observability.pin(window=30m, tags=["tilt", "model-v3"])

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add automated canary-eval gate that runs a lightweight eval harness at each step (JIRA: EVAL-2345)
- Decide on default tilt step size for global vs regional (proposal attached in Confluence link)
- Add customer-facing note template for CS to use if a public-facing regression is observed

Attachments / handy links:
- checklist template (copy to new release folder) -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/tilt-checklist-template
- incident runbook -> https://runbooks.redwood.ai/tilt-incident
- PR for tilt controller changes -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/pull/678

End notes: this is intentionally minimal and operator-centric. For the canonical release spec (with gating matrices and experiment logs) link to the release ticket (JIRA-RELEASE-8901). Keep this doc as the live-run checklist during the tilt window.

-- Priya (release engineer)
